title: Functorial finite twisted complexes and their homotopy categories
statement:
Use small dg categories and quasi-equivalences as in [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], with the cochain convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a small dg category $\mathcal B$, let $\operatorname{pretr}(\mathcal B)$ have objects finite expressions $T=(\bigoplus_{i=1}^m B_i[r_i],q)$, including $m=0$, where $r_i\in\mathbf Z$ and $q$ is a strictly upper triangular degree-$1$ matrix of shifted morphisms satisfying $dq+q^2=0$. Between $T=(\bigoplus B_i[r_i],q)$ and $T'=(\bigoplus B'_j[r'_j],q')$, the mapping complex is the matrix complex on the shifted mapping complexes of $\mathcal B$, with
$$d(f)=d_{\mathrm{shifted}}f+q'f-(-1)^{|f|}fq,$$
and composition is matrix multiplication with the shifted Koszul conventions. The embedding $\mathcal B\to\operatorname{pretr}(\mathcal B)$ on single unshifted summands is fully faithful on mapping complexes. Formal shifts and cones make $H^0\operatorname{pretr}(\mathcal B)$ a triangulated category: its distinguished triangles are those isomorphic to the formal cone triangles. A dg functor $F:\mathcal B\to\mathcal E$ induces a dg functor $\operatorname{pretr}(F)$ by applying $F$ to matrix entries; it commutes with formal zero, shifts and cones, and $H^0\operatorname{pretr}(F)$ is exact. The construction $\operatorname{pretr}$ preserves quasi-equivalences. If $\mathcal B$ is pretriangulated, meaning its representable modules are closed up to homotopy equivalence under zero, shifts and cones, the embedding $\mathcal B\to\operatorname{pretr}(\mathcal B)$ is a quasi-equivalence. These constructions are functorial in dg functors.
